memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they moved on from Bethel. While they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth and had great difficulty. And as she was having great difficulty in childbirth, the midwife said to her, 'Don't despair, for you have another son.' As she breathed her last—for she was dying—she named her son Ben-Oni. But his father named him Benjamin. So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem). Over her tomb Jacob set up a pillar, and to this day that pillar marks Rachel's tomb." - Gen 35:16-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joy and grief arrive together in this passage. Rachel, the wife Jacob loved so deeply, dies giving birth to her second son. With her last breath she names the baby Ben-Oni — "son of my sorrow." But Jacob gently renames him Benjamin — "son of my right hand," a name of honour and strength. In one heartbreaking moment, a mother's dying grief and a father's tender hope meet over the same little child.

This is life as we often know it — sorrow and hope woven tightly together. The same day can hold a death and a birth, a loss and a gift. Rachel's story reminds us that our deepest griefs and our sweetest blessings sometimes come hand in hand, and that God is present in both.

Notice how Jacob refuses to let his son be defined by sorrow alone. Rachel named him "son of my sorrow," but Jacob renamed him "son of my right hand." He chose to speak hope over grief. In our own losses, we too can grieve honestly and still hold on to hope, trusting that God can bring good even out of our sorrows.

And do not miss where this happened — on the way to Bethlehem. Centuries later, in that very town, another Son would be born, through whom God would turn the world's deepest sorrow into everlasting hope (Micah 5:2; Luke 2:4-7). Even here, in a graveside grief, God was quietly pointing toward the place of the world's greatest joy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where in my life have sorrow and hope come hand in hand?
2. Can I grieve honestly while still holding on to hope?
3. How does God's presence in Bethlehem speak hope into my sorrows?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, in seasons where grief and blessing come together, meet me with Your presence. Help me to grieve honestly yet hold on to hope, trusting You to bring joy even out of sorrow. Amen.
